title: The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy)

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Hanna Fund (1947.209)
image.license: Public domain. Released under the Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access program

altText: An autumn landscape with tall trees and small figures at work on a road below. The trees rise high in the picture and the scene is painted with energetic brushwork.

source.verifiedBy: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API record (title, artist, date, medium, credit line, description, did-you-know, CC0 status, image URL)

context: An oil painting by Vincent van Gogh, made in 1889 near Saint-Rémy in France and now in the Cleveland Museum of Art. The museum describes it as an autumnal landscape and notes that Van Gogh sometimes made what he called repetitions; conservation research shows the Cleveland painting is the first version of this composition.

descriptions.k: Look at the tall trees in this picture. Can you find the road? Can you find tiny workers near the trees? Point to the tallest part of the painting. What season do you think it is?
descriptions.g12: Vincent van Gogh painted tall trees and a road in the fall. Look for the small workers near the road and the big trees above them. His brushstrokes are bold and you can see them. How do the trees make the people look?
descriptions.g35: Vincent van Gogh painted this autumn landscape in 1889 in France. The title tells us that road menders, workers who repair roads, are at work beneath the large plane trees. The painting is made with bold, visible brushstrokes. How do the huge trees change the way you see the small workers?
descriptions.g68: Van Gogh painted this autumnal landscape in 1889 while staying near Saint-Rémy, France. The museum says he painted it during a stay at a psychiatric hospital, where his physician allowed him to paint outdoors, which eased his symptoms. Conservation research shows this is the first version of a composition he later repeated. How might the scale of the trees and the bold marks shape the mood of the picture?
descriptions.g910: Van Gogh made The Large Plane Trees (1889) near Saint-Rémy, where he was treated for severe depression and was allowed to paint outdoors, according to the museum. He called some later versions of his compositions repetitions, and the Phillips Collection holds one of this scene. How does the picture's balance of towering trees and small workers shape its mood, and how might knowing the circumstances affect how you read it?
descriptions.g1112: Painted in 1889 near Saint-Rémy, this autumn landscape is, according to the museum, the first version of a composition Van Gogh later repeated (a repetition is in the Phillips Collection). The museum connects his work there to his treatment for severe depression and permission to paint outdoors. How does the picture's structure, with large trees and small figures, support more than one reading, and how careful should we be in linking biography to what a painting means?

k.daily: Find the tall trees. Point to the tallest tree.
k.emotion: How does this fall picture make you feel? Does it feel quiet, busy or windy?
k.observation: Find the small workers by the road. How many can you spot?
k.analysis: The trees are big and the people are small. Which do you notice first?
k.line: Trace one tree trunk with your finger. Does it go up, down or across?
k.shape: Look for a tall shape and a flat shape. Which are the trees and which is the road?
k.color: Fall has many colors. Which fall colors do you see?
k.texture: The paint looks thick in places. Imagine touching it. What would it feel like?
k.space: Which tree looks closest to you, and which looks far away?
k.light: Where do you think the sun is in this picture?
k.meaning: What work do you think the people are doing on the road?
k.culture: Autumn is a season. What do you do in the fall?
k.technique: Van Gogh used short, thick strokes. Where can you find some that look like little lines?
k.personal: If you could stand on this road, which way would you walk?
k.critical: What is your favorite tree near where you live?

g12.daily: Why do you think Van Gogh made the trees so large and the workers so small?
g12.emotion: What feeling do the fall colors give you, calm or lively?
g12.observation: List five things you can find in the picture, starting with the trees.
g12.analysis: Why do your eyes keep going to the tall trunks?
g12.line: How do the lines of the tree trunks and the road lead your eyes through the painting?
g12.shape: Which shapes are tall, which are round and which are flat in this scene?
g12.color: What fall colors can you find, and how do they feel together?
g12.texture: How did the painter use thick paint to make the leaves and bark look rough?
g12.space: How can you tell that the road goes back into the distance?
g12.light: Where does light shine on the trees, and where is it darker?
g12.meaning: What story could you tell about the workers fixing the road?
g12.culture: Road menders fixed roads by hand long ago. What do you think their work was like?
g12.technique: Van Gogh used short strokes of paint side by side. What do they make the leaves look like?
g12.personal: What would you paint if you could sit under these trees for a day?
g12.critical: How would the painting feel different if it showed a summer day instead?

g35.daily: How does Van Gogh use the huge size of the plane trees to make the road menders look small?
g35.emotion: What mood do the autumn colors and strong brushwork create, and which details support it?
g35.observation: Choose one tree. Describe its trunk, branches and leaves, and how the paint was applied.
g35.analysis: How do the vertical trunks and the road work together to organize the picture?
g35.line: How do the directions of the brushstrokes in the trunks and leaves give the scene energy?
g35.shape: How do the tall, columnlike trunks contrast with the small shapes of the workers?
g35.color: How do warm and cool colors work together to show an autumn day?
g35.texture: How does the thick, visible paint make the picture feel full of movement?
g35.space: How does Van Gogh show the road going back into the distance past the big trees?
g35.light: How does the painter use light and shadow to show the shape of the trees?
g35.meaning: What might the road menders and the giant trees tell us about people and nature?
g35.culture: Why might a painter in 1889 choose workers repairing a road as a subject?
g35.technique: How does using short, bold strokes change the feel of the painting compared with smooth blending?
g35.personal: What place outdoors do you know well, and how would you paint it so people could feel it?
g35.critical: How is looking at this painting different from looking at a photograph of trees in autumn?

g910.daily: How does the contrast of towering trees and small figures shape the viewer's sense of scale and mood?
g910.emotion: How do color choices and the bold surface of the paint establish an emotional tone for the autumn landscape?
g910.observation: Compare the way Van Gogh paints the trunks, the leaves and the road. What differences in handling do you see?
g910.analysis: How do the vertical trunks create a rhythm and frame the figures below?
g910.line: How do the directional marks in the foliage and trunks make the painting feel active rather than still?
g910.shape: How do the massive trunk forms contrast with the smaller, more irregular forms of the workers and the road?
g910.color: How does color contrast, between warm autumn hues and cooler notes, build unity and interest?
g910.texture: How does the thick, visible paint make the picture an object as well as an image?
g910.space: How does the arrangement of trunks, branches and road lead the viewer into depth while also flattening the picture?
g910.light: How does the handling of light and shadow help give the trees weight and presence?
g910.meaning: The museum notes this is the first version of a composition Van Gogh repeated. What might repeating a composition reveal about his goals?
g910.culture: How might the museum's note that his physician allowed him to paint outdoors affect how you read the scene?
g910.technique: How would working in oil on fabric outdoors affect how quickly and how boldly he could paint?
g910.personal: How do you decide how much a painter's life should shape your reading of a painting?
g910.critical: How would you test whether the mood of this painting comes from the trees themselves or from the way the paint is applied?

g1112.daily: How does the monumentality of the trees relative to the figures suggest a relationship between human labor and the natural world, and what other readings are possible?
g1112.emotion: How might Van Gogh's color relationships and surface treatment function as expressive devices rather than descriptive ones?
g1112.observation: Where does the painting shift between observation of a place and invention of a mood, and how can you tell?
g1112.analysis: How does the vertical emphasis of the composition structure the picture and compress or expand the sense of space?
g1112.line: How does the directional rhythm of the brushwork organize the picture where outline does not?
g1112.shape: How do the repeated columnar forms of the trunks relate to the smaller irregular forms of the workers in building meaning?
g1112.color: How might the contrast between warm and cool areas heighten the expressive intensity of the scene without losing a sense of a real place?
g1112.texture: How does the thick, layered paint participate in the picture's meaning as well as its appearance?
g1112.space: How does the spatial construction balance a plausible road and woodland with a flattened, patterned surface?
g1112.light: How might light and shadow here function as formal structure and as expressive tone?
g1112.meaning: The museum identifies this as the first version of a composition later repeated, with a version at the Phillips Collection. What does repetition suggest about how Van Gogh thought about a subject?
g1112.culture: The museum links his stay at a psychiatric hospital with permission to paint outdoors. How should a viewer weigh that context against what the painting itself shows?
g1112.technique: How might the circumstances of making a painting in 1889 at Saint-Rémy affect what we expect it to show, and where might those expectations mislead us?
g1112.personal: How does knowing about an artist's health alter, or fail to alter, your response to a landscape?
g1112.critical: What would a rigorous argument look like for reading this painting as formal experiment, and another for reading it as emotional expression? Which does the evidence support better?

g68.daily: What choices make these trees feel so powerful, and which one affects you most?
g68.emotion: How do the autumn colors and the thick brushwork shape the mood, and what words would you use for it?
g68.observation: Look closely at the road menders. What can you tell about them, and what is hard to tell?
g68.analysis: How do the tall trunks and the small figures create balance in the composition?
g68.line: How do the lines of the trunks, branches and road lead your eye around the painting?
g68.shape: How do the large, columnlike trunks compare with the smaller shapes of the workers?
g68.color: How do warm and cool colors set beside each other help create an autumn atmosphere?
g68.texture: How do the thick, visible strokes make the leaves, bark and road feel different from each other?
g68.space: How does Van Gogh show the road and trees moving back into distance?
g68.light: How do light and shadow give the trees weight, and where is the strongest contrast?
g68.meaning: What might the contrast between very large trees and small workers suggest about people and nature?
g68.culture: The museum notes that his physician allowed him to paint outdoors. Why might that detail matter when you look at this scene?
g68.technique: The museum says this is the first version of a composition he repeated. What might he gain from painting it again?
g68.personal: Which outdoor place would you paint to show how it feels to be there? Which colors would you choose?
g68.critical: How could you tell whether the energy in this painting comes from the subject or from how it is painted?

teacherNote.context: An oil painting made in 1889 by Vincent van Gogh near Saint-Rémy, France, now in the Cleveland Museum of Art. It is an autumn landscape with large plane trees and workers repairing a road.
directions: Have students draw a tall tree with small people beneath it and discuss how scale changes the mood.
Ask students to practice short, directional brushstrokes with paint or markers to show bark and leaves.
For older students, discuss how much an artist's life should influence our reading of a painting. The museum text mentions a psychiatric hospital; treat this respectfully and factually.
